result:
The minimum is 4040, i.e. 2n − 4 with n = 2022. I verified the construction and small cases (n = 4, 5) by hand. The general lower bound I did not prove; I am relying on it matching the pattern.

**Construction.** Take two users a and b, and make each of the other n − 2 users a friend of both a and b. This uses 2(n − 2) = 2n − 4 friendships.
- Any two of the other users have a and b as common friends, so they can all become friends with each other.
- Then a and b share every other user as a common friend, so they can become friends too.

Every pair ends up as friends, so this starting graph works.

**Small cases supporting minimality.**
- For n = 4, the 4-cycle with 4 = 2·4 − 4 edges works. A graph with 3 edges cannot work, because a tree has no pair with two common friends.
- For n = 5, a graph with 5 edges would need a 4-cycle to make any first move, so it would be a 4-cycle plus one pendant user. The 4-cycle fills in to K₄, but the pendant user has only one friend, so it never gains a pair with two common friends. Hence 6 = 2·5 − 4 edges are needed.

For n = 2022 this gives 2·2022 − 4 = 4040.

ANSWER: 4040
